Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

hdf5lib 2.2.0.1

  • Blosc and Blosc2 multi-threading now pays off. The Blosc2 filter keeps its compression and decompression contexts, and their worker threads, alive between chunks instead of starting a new thread pool for every chunk; Blosc (v1) runs through c-blosc’s persistent global pool when threads are requested. Both filters still default to one thread.
  • New C API hdf5lib_set_blosc_nthreads() / hdf5lib_get_blosc_nthreads() in hdf5lib.h sets the Blosc and Blosc2 thread count. The BLOSC_NTHREADS environment variable, which Blosc (v1) previously ignored, now applies to both filters and takes precedence, though the function is the better choice (see the compression article).
  • New C API hdf5lib_set_blosc2() in hdf5lib.h adds the Blosc2 filter to a dataset creation property list from a codec, compression level, pre-filters and meta value, so callers no longer work out the packed cd_values[0] by hand. hdf5lib.h also names the codecs and pre-filters (HDF5LIB_BLOSC2_ZSTD, HDF5LIB_BLOSC2_BITSHUFFLE and so on), and a negative meta value, such as ZFP accuracy’s exponent, is passed as it is.
  • hdf5lib.h now declares the ZFP helpers H5Pset_zfp_rate(), H5Pset_zfp_precision(), H5Pset_zfp_accuracy(), H5Pset_zfp_expert() and H5Pset_zfp_reversible(), so callers no longer need to write extern declarations for them. Existing extern declarations still compile.
  • ZFP no longer silently corrupts NaN, NA, and Inf values. The standalone ZFP filter (except in reversible mode) and Blosc2’s ZFP codecs now refuse chunks that hold them, so an optional filter stores those chunks unfiltered and a mandatory one fails the write.
  • Blosc2 datasets with 1-D chunks (or more than 16 dimensions) are now readable by h5py with hdf5plugin. The filter used to record a chunk rank of 1 (or 0) in its parameters, which hdf5plugin’s Blosc2 filter rejects; it now stores the reference filter’s seven values for such chunks. Datasets already written by hdf5lib 2.2.0.0 and earlier keep their old parameters: hdf5lib still reads them, but hdf5plugin cannot, so rewrite them to share them with Python.
  • Blosc2 (32026) has a new cd_values layout, in which every slot holds what the reference HDF5-Blosc2 filter keeps there. cd_values[5] is now the last pre-filter as a single Blosc2 filter code (0 none, 1 shuffle, 2 bitshuffle, 3 delta, 4 trunc-prec), and nothing follows the chunk shape. hdf5lib’s own settings, the pre-filter bitmask and the meta value (trunc-prec’s precision, NDLZ’s cell size or the ZFP codecs’ parameter), are packed into cd_values[0], where the reference keeps a revision number it never reads: 0xB2100001 + (bitmask << 16) + (meta << 8). hdf5plugin read the old bitmask as a filter code, so it took delta (4) for trunc-prec and rejected pipelines such as delta + bitshuffle (6); it now describes hdf5lib’s datasets by their last pre-filter, and h5py can append to them. Pass the new form, 7 values, to H5Pset_filter(). The old form, with cd_values[0] = 0, the bitmask in cd_values[5] and the meta value as an 8th value, is still accepted and stored in the new layout. Creation property lists copied from datasets that earlier versions or the reference filter wrote are converted too, and chunks appended to those datasets keep their settings. hdf5lib used to read a reference dataset’s cd_values[5] as a bitmask when appending to it, running delta (3) as bitshuffle. See the compression article for the layout and for what h5py does with each kind of dataset.
  • Patched the bundled ZFP to remove undefined behaviour that UBSan reports. Its lifting transforms now do their arithmetic in unsigned integers instead of relying on signed overflow and left shifts of negative values. Reversible mode no longer converts NaN or Inf to an integer when it tests whether a block can be stored exactly. Output is bit-for-bit unchanged.
  • The ZFP filter no longer leaks a datatype ID for every dataset it is applied to.
  • An optional ZFP filter on chunks that ZFP cannot compress now leaves every chunk unfiltered by design. This covers a single value, more than four dimensions longer than one, items other than 4 or 8 bytes, and data in non-native byte order. The filter used to record no parameters for some of these chunks and then read past them, fail H5Dcreate2() for others, and compress byte-swapped data as though it were native, which corrupted it. It now records parameters that make it refuse every chunk, and it refuses chunks whose parameters are missing, as in datasets earlier versions wrote this way. A mandatory ZFP filter still makes H5Dcreate2() fail on such chunks.
  • ZFP’s set_local callback now reports errors such as an invalid mode instead of succeeding without recording parameters. A dataset created from another ZFP dataset’s creation property list, as h5repack creates them, now gets a ZFP header for its own chunks in the same mode. It used to inherit the original’s header, which miscompressed chunks of a different shape or type.
  • Blosc2’s truncate-precision pre-filter (bitmask 8) now applies only to native-order float32 and float64 data, and arrays of them; for other datatypes the flag is dropped. It used to zero the low bits of any 4- or 8-byte item: integers and 8-byte compound records were corrupted (keeping 10 bits, every int32 below 8192 read back as 0), and chunks of other item sizes failed. A precision that Blosc2 cannot apply (keeping 0 bits, or dropping the whole mantissa) now makes H5Dcreate2() fail instead of every chunk, and keeping more bits than the mantissa holds keeps them all. Datasets created by earlier versions keep the flag, so chunks written to them later are still truncated.
  • A Blosc2 dataset created from another’s creation property list, as h5repack creates them, now keeps the original’s meta value (truncation precision, or the ZFP codecs’ parameter). For chunks with two or more dimensions the filter took the stored chunk rank for it, so a 2-D copy kept 2 bits of precision, or relaxed ZFP’s accuracy to 10^2. The meta value is now stored in cd_values[0], away from the chunk shape.
  • Blosc2’s ZFP codecs (33 to 35) no longer silently corrupt data that is not native-order float32 or float64. They compressed integers and byte-swapped floats as though they were native floats, and the values read back as garbage (small integers as 0) without any error. A mandatory filter now makes H5Dcreate2() fail on such data. An optional one stores it unfiltered: it records compression level 255, which makes every Blosc2 filter (hdf5plugin’s included) refuse each chunk. A compression level above 9 now makes H5Dcreate2() fail instead of every chunk.
  • The read-only BitRound shim now sits on BitRound’s registered filter ID, 32032. It used to claim 32024, which belongs to SZ3. Registering hdf5lib’s filters then made SZ3 datasets unreadable and stopped HDF5 from loading a real SZ3 plugin. The shim on 32023, formerly called BitShave, is now named for Granular BitRound, the quantizer registered under that ID.
  • hdf5lib_destroy_all_filters() now also unregisters the BitGroom, Granular BitRound, and BitRound read shims that hdf5lib_register_all_filters() registers.
  • Blosc2 no longer loses data when a chunk’s bytes don’t match the chunk geometry it records. Three cases hit this: an array datatype with 2-D or larger chunks, NDLZ with an array datatype, and a filter that changes a chunk’s size (Fletcher32 or scale-offset) running before Blosc2. Only part of each chunk was compressed, so writes succeeded and every read failed. Array datatypes are now recorded without B2ND geometry, and a chunk whose size doesn’t match its geometry falls back to plain Blosc2, as the reference filter does.
  • Blosc2’s ZFP codecs no longer fail every chunk with a rank above 4 or a dimension under 4, shapes that c-blosc2’s ZFP codec rejects. Such chunks now use 1-D ZFP. A chunk of fewer than 4 values is handled like a datatype ZFP can’t take. Blosc2 now also reads datasets whose filter parameters hold fewer than 7 values, as the reference filter writes them for 1-D chunks.
  • Every filter now fails cleanly on a truncated or corrupt chunk. Previously bzip2 hung, Snappy returned an uninitialized tail, LZ4 didn’t check each block’s decoded length, and Blosc, Bitshuffle and ZFP could read past the end of the chunk.
  • The Snappy filter (32003) now writes chunks in the layout of snappy-cuda, the filter that HDF5’s registry assigns that ID to, so the two can read each other’s files. A chunk holds the uncompressed length and a 32 KiB block size as varints, then each block as a 4-byte little-endian length and its raw Snappy data. The filter used to write one raw Snappy stream per chunk, which snappy-cuda can’t read. It reads both layouts, snappy-cuda’s at any block size, and still uses only the bundled csnappy, so no CUDA is needed. hdf5lib 2.2.0.0 and earlier can’t read Snappy chunks written by this version. Blosc’s snappy codec is a different container (filter 32001) and remains the way to share Snappy-compressed data with h5py and hdf5plugin, which have no 32003 filter.
  • Snappy now refuses chunks of about 3.4 GB or more, whose worst-case compressed size overflowed its output buffer. LZF refuses chunks of 4 GB or more, which it used to truncate silently; HDF5 2.x allows chunks that large.
  • ZFP now byte-swaps data before compressing chunks appended to a dataset written on a machine of the other byte order, matching how such chunks are read. It refuses a chunk whose size differs from what its ZFP header describes, where it used to read past the chunk. Chunk dimensions too large for ZFP’s header are now treated like other chunks ZFP can’t take, so an optional filter declines them instead of failing H5Dcreate2(). A dataset created from a declined dataset’s creation property list is declined again instead of failing.
  • Bitshuffle: a dataset created from another Bitshuffle dataset’s creation property list, as h5repack creates them, now keeps its codec. set_local used to shift the copied parameters again, so every chunk failed. A block size that isn’t a multiple of 8, or an unknown codec, now makes H5Dcreate2() fail instead of every chunk. An element size of 0 no longer divides by zero. Unknown codec IDs in existing files are read as plain bitshuffle, as the reference filter reads them.
  • The read-only BitGroom, Granular BitRound and BitRound shims are now registered only for IDs no other filter has, such as a real plugin found through HDF5_PLUGIN_PATH, which can also write. hdf5lib_destroy_all_filters() unregisters only the shims it registered.
  • Compiled code no longer refers to the C library’s stderr, which R CMD check flags in packages that link hdf5lib. The Blosc filter now reports errors only through HDF5’s error stack, and bzip2 is built with BZ_NO_STDIO. c-blosc2’s BLOSC_TRACE and BLOSC_INFO messages are compiled out, because they could run on Blosc worker threads, where R’s console can’t be used.
  • The smoke tests now read data back through a fresh dataset handle, so every chunk is decompressed rather than served from HDF5’s chunk cache.
  • Corrected the Blosc2 NDLZ codec ID in the compression article (32, not 11), corrected its claims about h5py interoperability, and documented the threading and non-finite behaviour. The interoperability tests now cover 1-D and high-rank Blosc2 chunks, Blosc2’s ZFP and NDLZ codecs, and the old and new Blosc2 cd_values forms, and check that hdf5plugin describes hdf5lib’s Blosc2 datasets and that h5py can append to them.

hdf5lib 2.2.0.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-09

  • Enables installation to read-only directories.
  • Dependency updates: HDF5 (2.1.1 to 2.2.0), c-blosc2 (2.23.1 to 3.3.3), and libaec (1.1.6 to 1.1.7).

hdf5lib 2.1.1.2

CRAN release: 2026-07-21

  • Patch c-blosc2-2.23.1/blosc/frame.c for strncpy warnings on GCC 16.

hdf5lib 2.1.1.1

CRAN release: 2026-05-15

  • Respect LD and STRIP env vars during linking step (allows cross-platform builds).
  • Patched strncpy warnings introduced by GCC 16 in src/H5FDsplitter.c.

hdf5lib 2.1.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-04-02

  • Updated HDF5 to 2.1.1.
  • Migrated from zlib to zlib-ng for gzip/deflate compression.
  • Added Szip (libaec), Bzip2, LZF, LZ4, Zstandard (Zstd), Snappy, Bitshuffle, ZFP, Blosc, and Blosc2.

hdf5lib 2.0.0.6

CRAN release: 2026-02-19

  • Accept decimal values for api argument in c_flags() and ld_flags().
  • New hdf5lib hex logo.
  • Updated documentation.

hdf5lib 2.0.0.5

CRAN release: 2026-01-14

  • Patched misaligned address in HDF5’s H5Tconv_enum.c file.

hdf5lib 2.0.0.4

CRAN release: 2025-12-22

  • Patched zlib win32/Makefile.gcc for conda-forge compatibility.

hdf5lib 2.0.0.3

CRAN release: 2025-12-14

  • Patched misaligned address in HDF5’s H5Tvlen.c file.
  • Fix for Alpine Linux (musl) CRAN check.
  • Clarified that c_flags() and ld_flags’s api argument should be numeric.

hdf5lib 2.0.0.2

CRAN release: 2025-12-02

  • Updated to HDF5 2.0.0
  • Added api argument to c_flags to control exposed HDF5 API.
  • Customized HDF5 build configuration for R environment.

hdf5lib 1.14.6.9

  • Added additional CPPFLAGS include directories needed by Fedora builders.
  • Automated build testing using rhub github actions.

hdf5lib 1.14.6.8

CRAN release: 2025-11-19

  • Fixed compiler flags for Fedora builders.
  • Renamed libhdf5.a to libhdf5z.a eliminate ambiguity with system libraries.
  • Paths returned by c_flags() and ld_flags() are only quoted when necessary.

hdf5lib 1.14.6.7

CRAN release: 2025-11-17

  • Corrected link to inst/COPYRIGHTS.

hdf5lib 1.14.6.6

  • Added HDF5 and zlib copyright holders to DESCRIPTION.

hdf5lib 1.14.6.5

  • Fixed compilation error identified on CRAN’s Fedora builders.

hdf5lib 1.14.6.4

CRAN release: 2025-11-10

  • Initial CRAN submission.
